chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Amr al-Zayyat from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever dies in Al-Madinah, Allah, Exalted and Mighty, will resurrect him among the trustworthy (Al-Aminin) on the Day of Resurrection."
Among them are Yahya ibn Habib, Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj. This is from the speech of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id al-Zayyat.

key_terms.الْأَمِينِينَ: Al-Aminin (the trustworthy, a title often associated with the Prophet and his followers)
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: Al-Madinah (the city, specifically referring to Medina)
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Azza wa Jalla (Exalted and Mighty, an honorific for Allah)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for dying in Al-Madinah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, 'Al-Madinah' in this context is often interpreted specifically as Najaf, the burial place of Imam Ali (AS), rather than the general city of Medina, emphasizing the virtue of dying near the Ahl al-Bayt. The promise of being resurrected among 'Al-Aminin' (the trustworthy) underscores the spiritual purity and divine favor associated with proximity to the Imams. This narration is found in the chapter detailing the merits of specific mosques and burial sites, linking physical location to eschatological status.
